Onset ordering is now internally consistent: 11:01:25Z partner connect timeout → 11:01Z gateway bucket → 11:02:45Z first order-service error (~1m20s later). The load-induced alternative is positively contradicted: F29/F30 show flat request volume (gateway 245-292 req/s, order-service 203-247 req/s) with no step at 11:01Z while the affected fraction jumps discontinuously to a constant ~44-48%, i.e. a fixed-fraction, load-independent upstream defect. Remaining weaknesses are real but not blocking and are reflected in the confidence cap: (a) exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false and no partner-side source exists in this toolset (F22, T5), so the partner origin is inferred from the caller's own telemetry — F10/F11/F25/F26 are all exchange-gateway-owned; (b) the propagation hop order-service→exchange-gateway synchronous-with-no-fallback remains an assumption, never source/trace-verified; (c) payment/inventory and shared-component (ledger-db/redis/kafka) health were never queried, so the blast-radius list is not exhaustively bounded. Critically, none of these gaps could reorder the leading hypotheses: they are all consistent with H1, and every competing origin (H2 rollback-insensitive defect, H4 1h40m-stale config) is already contradicted by data in hand rather than merely unqueried. Confidence capped at 0.85 rather than higher because the deepest hop rests on a single, non-independent telemetry source and one unverified propagation assumption. The reporter's ongoing rollback is harmless and consistent.

tasks.objective: Establish the true symptom onset time and blast radius: plot order-service error rate and 504 latency from 06:00Z to now to pinpoint when failures began (relative to the v2.15.2 rollout), confirm whether the 30% error rate is real and sustained, and determine which error signatures dominate. Critically, check whether other services (especially order-service's downstream dependencies like payment/inventory/DB) show degradation or timeouts in the same window, and whether the failures are endpoint- or caller-specific. Report the exact onset timestamp and the list of genuinely affected services.
tasks.answer: Order-service failures began sharply at ~11:00Z (first error log 11:02:45Z), coincident with — not clearly before — the v2.15.2 rollout, and the 30% error rate is real and sustained (~31% avg through 12:52Z). The failures are dominated by ONE signature: order-service→exchange-gateway calls returning 504 Gateway Timeout on placeOrder. The real upstream origin is below exchange-gateway: it shows 5s upstream connect timeouts to api.exchange-partner.example and 503s from exchange-api, with exchange-gateway error rate (~43%) actually HIGHER and starting EARLIER (10:58Z) than order-service's. So blast radius: order-service and exchange-gateway are both genuinely affected; the external exchange partner API is the deepest visible degradation point. I could not confirm payment/inventory status (queries hit the call limit).

critiques.summary: Round-1's single blocking issue — the 3-minute timing inversion and whether the gateway's degradation was upstream-driven (partner) vs. load-induced by the 10:48Z order-service deploy — has been resolved by per-minute data. F25/F26 show gateway error_rate and upstream_error_rate flat at baseline (0.25/0.27/0.12%) through 10:58-11:00Z, then a single-minute step to 44-45% at the 11:01Z bucket; F27 (truncated=false, single match) shows the first upstream connect timeout at 11:01:25Z, so the previously cited 10:58Z onset was indeed a coarse-bucket artifact. Onset ordering is now internally consistent: 11:01:25Z partner connect timeout → 11:01Z gateway bucket → 11:02:45Z first order-service error (~1m20s later). The load-induced alternative is positively contradicted: F29/F30 show flat request volume (gateway 245-292 req/s, order-service 203-247 req/s) with no step at 11:01Z while the affected fraction jumps discontinuously to a constant ~44-48%, i.e. a fixed-fraction, load-independent upstream defect. H2 is killed by mechanism (an order-service code defect cannot emit 5000ms connect timeouts to a vendor host) AND by outcome (rollback at 11:16Z left errors at 31.42% through 12:52Z, F16). H3/H4 are dismissed on evidence, not assumption: the dominant/earliest signature is external-host connect timeouts on a path with no shared datastore between order-service and exchange-gateway (F15), and the only config change (pricing-engine TTL, 09:20Z) sits 1h40m earlier on a different branch with a fully quiet interval. Remaining weaknesses are real but not blocking and are reflected in the confidence cap: (a) exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false and no partner-side source exists in this toolset (F22, T5), so the partner origin is inferred from the caller's own telemetry — F10/F11/F25/F26 are all exchange-gateway-owned; (b) the propagation hop order-service→exchange-gateway synchronous-with-no-fallback remains an assumption, never source/trace-verified; (c) payment/inventory and shared-component (ledger-db/redis/kafka) health were never queried, so the blast-radius list is not exhaustively bounded. Critically, none of these gaps could reorder the leading hypotheses: they are all consistent with H1, and every competing origin (H2 rollback-insensitive defect, H4 1h40m-stale config) is already contradicted by data in hand rather than merely unqueried. Confidence capped at 0.85 rather than higher because the deepest hop rests on a single, non-independent telemetry source and one unverified propagation assumption. The reporter's ongoing rollback is harmless and consistent.

challenges.issue: The deepest causal hop (partner-side failure) rests entirely on exchange-gateway's own telemetry (F10/F11/F25/F26/F27). exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false (F22) and T5 confirmed no independent partner-side status/change source exists in this toolset. 'Partner' vs 'exchange-gateway's own connection/DNS layer' is therefore not source-verified — though both share the same fix (engage the vendor; gateway received zero changes in 48h, F21). This is why the cap stays at 0.85, not higher.

The propagation hop 'order-service calls exchange-gateway synchronously on placeOrder with no short-enough fallback/timeout' is explicitly an ASSUMED entry — no order-service or exchange-gateway source/trace was reviewed. It is corroborated only indirectly (the single dominant signature is exchange-gateway 504 on placeOrder, F9; p99 tracks the 5s timeout, F8).

Blast radius is not exhaustively bounded: payment-service/inventory-service logs were never retrieved (budget_exhausted) and no per-component metrics for ledger-db/redis-cache/kafka were queried. These are gaps, not disconfirmations — the observed signature (external-host connect timeouts, fixed 44-48% fraction, no shared datastore in path) does not connect to them, so they cannot outrank H1.

F18 retains v2.15.2 as the temporally closest change (12 min before onset). This is now decisively outweighed: the earliest degradation is on a component with zero changes in 48h (F21), and rollback left errors flat at 31.42% (F16). No further work needed.

Rejection cites 'no shared-component error in any collected log' while the gaps concede shared-component metrics were never queried — the dismissal leans partly on absence of evidence. Not blocking: the mechanism does not connect to the observed external-host timeout signature.
